title: Development of a Doubled Haploid Mapping Population of Pyropia yezoensis
author: Linbin Huang
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.x3vfqn6

steps.title: Maintain stock conchocelis cultures
steps.instruction: Keep free‑living conchocelis of Py‑LS and Py‑HT in 250 mL SEBC bottles containing 200 mL natural seawater‑MES medium at 19 °C under 10 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹ (10:14 LD); aerate and renew 50 % of the medium every 10–12 months.

steps.title: Induce conchosporangia in Petri dish
steps.instruction: Sample ~10 µg conchocelis from the stock, place in a 90 mm Petri dish and incubate at 23 °C under 20 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹ (10:14 LD) until conchosporangia appear.

steps.title: Transfer to flask and attach conchospores
steps.instruction: Move the conchocelis with conchosporangia into a 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask containing 200 mL medium, aerate, and incubate at 19 °C under 40 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹ (10:14 LD); add ~3 cm vinylon monofilaments for conchospore attachment.

steps.title: Obtain conchospore germlings
steps.instruction: Transfer the monofilaments bearing attached conchospores to a fresh flask with the same conditions; culture until conchospore germlings (gametophytic blades) develop. Renew medium 50 % every 5 days.

steps.title: Isolate blades and co‑culture for fertilization
steps.instruction: When blades reach 1–2 cm, detach them from monofilaments and culture each blade individually in its own flask. When spermatangia appear but before spermatia release, cut the upper peripheral portion of one Py‑HT blade and one Py‑LS blade and co‑culture them until carposporangia form.

steps.title: Culture fertilized blade to mature carposporangia
steps.instruction: Transfer the fertilized blade to a 500 mL flask containing 450 mL medium and culture under the same temperature and light conditions until carposporangia mature.

steps.title: Release carpospores from dried blade
steps.instruction: Dry the blade with mature carposporangia in shade at 19 °C, then immerse it in a 90 mm Petri dish with 50 mL medium for 1 hour to induce carpospore release; return the blade to a flask for repeated releases over subsequent days.

steps.title: Grow carpospores to conchocelis colonies
steps.instruction: Incubate released carpospores in 90 mm Petri dishes at 19 °C under 20 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹ (14:10 LD) until conchocelis colonies become microscopically distinguishable; pick wild‑type colored colonies with a fine Pasteur pipette and transfer to Petri dishes or test tubes. Renew medium only after colonies become macroscopic.

steps.title: Induce conchosporangia in heterozygous conchocelis
steps.instruction: After ~3 months, when wild‑type conchocelis clumps reach ~10 mm diameter, culture them at 23 °C under 30 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹ (10:14 LD) to induce conchosporangia.

steps.title: Identify heterozygous conchocelis by F1 coloration
steps.instruction: ~3 weeks later, detach F₁ gametophytic blades from monofilaments with a surgical blade, examine color sectors microscopically; if >90 % of blades from a conchocelis are 2–4 color‑sectored, classify that conchocelis as a heterozygote.

steps.title: Generate DH strains from four‑color blades
steps.instruction: Select four‑color sectored mosaic blades, cut each blade into four color sectors along sector boundaries, and culture each sector separately. A doubled‑haploid (DH) strain is obtained when a self‑fertilized sector releases a carpospore that develops into a single conchocelis.

steps.title: Culture DH strain gametophytic blades
steps.instruction: Collect conchospores of each of the 148 DH strains individually, attach them to vinylon monofilaments, and culture in 300 mL flasks with 250 mL medium at 19 °C under 28–30 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹ (14:10 LD). Renew 50 % of the medium every 10 days; after 30 days detach the blades.

steps.title: Sequentially transfer blades to larger flasks
steps.instruction: Randomly pick 100 intact blades (with holdfasts and tips) and move them to a 600 mL flask containing 500 mL medium (half old, half new) under 38–40 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹. After 5 days, select 50 blades (35‑day‑old) and renew half the medium. After another 5 days, transfer 30 blades (40‑day‑old) to a 1200 mL flask with 1000 mL medium (half old, half new); renew 50 % of the medium every 5 days.

steps.title: Measure blade dimensions at 40 days
steps.instruction: Record length (holdfast to tip), width (widest part), and fresh weight (after surface water removed with a paper towel) of the 40‑day‑old blades (L40, W40, FW40).

steps.title: Measure and calculate growth rates at 50 days
steps.instruction: Ten days later (50 days), measure length, width, and fresh weight (L50, W50, FW50). Compute specific growth rates: LGR = (ln L50 – ln L40)/10, WGR = (ln W50 – ln W40)/10, FWGR = (ln FW50 – ln FW40)/10.
